Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this packet. I did not try to identify the work or author. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..022 in this packet directory, plus a directory listing and an image-size check (sips) of my own packet files. I did nothing beyond the stated rules.

Conventions: (x) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unread; [...] = text lost off the cut edge of the strip. Line numbers count from the top of the named image. Pencil shelfmarks/foliation in a modern hand (e.g. "Stams, STA, Frag. 103_1r", "Hs 228") were seen and are not transcribed as text.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001 = face A overview; image-012 = face B overview)
======================================================================
Observations:
- Each face shows FOUR separate vertical parchment strips laid side by side. Each strip carries the inner edge of one text column, a blank vertical band (intercolumnium, with ruled bounding lines), and the outer edge of a second column. Both columns are cut on the outside, so every line loses letters on one side: left column loses its line-beginnings, right column loses its line-endings.
- Gothic textualis (fairly small, compressed, heavily abbreviated) in brown-black ink; about 17-18 lines visible per strip in each crop.
- Red rubrics in the text column and large red initials (H/E-shaped, P, A, S/O-shaped, I with long tail/descender into the intercolumn). A red paragraph mark sits before line-ends (e.g. "abia").
- Small parchment binding tabs/guards are stuck on strip 1 of face A and strip 1 of face B. Wormholes and losses throughout. Face B strip 1 is much abraded, with brown offset/ghost text.
- No glosses or marginal additions seen. Text appears to be continuous narrative prose with chapter rubrics of the form "De X z Y", plus one rubric "Incidentia".
- Strip order in the photographs is as laid out by the photographer; I have not tried to reconstruct the original column order or which strip backs which.

Tentative interpretation (not identification): continuous prose narrative on Old Testament kings and prophets, with chronological cross-references ("anno xxvii asa"), named authorities ("ut ait iosephus", "herodotus"? , "s(ecundu)m quosdam") and an "Incidentia" section. Possibly a historical/biblical compendium; I do not infer more.

Areas selected: all eight strip-columns on face A (tiles 002-011) and on face B (tiles 013-022). Least legible: face B strip 1 both columns (tiles 013, 018, 019), and the lower part of face A strip 3 right column (tile 010). Overlap: each strip appears in two vertically stacked tiles (top/bottom) and neighbouring tiles share 2-4 lines; repeated lines are noted, not double-counted.
